Origin harbour, intermediate anchorage, and destination harbour reference locations

metadata.goal: Analyze the sailing patterns of a single vessel from its given trajectories, identify its typical voyage processes, and detect anomalous trajectories that depart from those processes.
metadata.category: single-vessel voyage staging and process anomaly detection
metadata.header: Single-Vessel Sailing Stages and a Direct-Nonstop Anomaly
metadata.dataset_description: This open-water case uses AIS-like point fields available in Danish AIS, including SOG, COG, heading, ROT, and navigational status. It is not geographically tied to Kattegat: the task concerns trajectory staging across repeated voyages of one vessel. The case design follows SteadySeg's framing of maritime trajectory staging as the segmentation and classification of changing navigational-status processes, with stable trajectories expected to have few state transitions.
metadata.source_note: Methodological inspiration: Qiu et al., SteadySeg: Improving maritime trajectory staging by steadiness recognition, Ocean Engineering 318 (2025), 120136. The points and harbour names are provided for this case.

insight_list.insight: The typical voyage process is stable across 11 trajectories: Under way using engine when leaving Harbour Orion, followed by an intermediate At anchor stage, Under way sailing, Restricted manoeuvrability on the approach to Harbour Lyra, and At anchor after arrival.

plot.title: Repeated Voyage Stage Sequence
plot.description: Each row is one normal voyage. Its colored runs show the same five-stage status sequence.

insight_list.question: What navigational-status sequence recurs across this vessel's repeated voyages, and where are its stable stage boundaries?
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
points = pd.read_csv(dataset_path)

insight_list.insight: Every normal transition from Under way sailing to Restricted manoeuvrability contains a large course change. The turn redirects the vessel from its eastbound transit toward Harbour Lyra, where the final anchoring stage occurs.

plot.title: Approach Turn Course Change
plot.description: The map locates the common approach turn; the paired COG points quantify its repeated change for each normal voyage.

insight_list.question: How does course change at the transition from Under way sailing to Restricted manoeuvrability, and how is that change positioned relative to the destination harbour?

insight_list.insight: voyage_12_direct_nonstop is the sole process anomaly. It does not anchor at the intermediate anchorage before arriving at Harbour Lyra, and its mean SOG is higher than for the typical voyages (10.19 versus 7.29 knots). Its turning point is farther north, so the final turn is milder and its mean absolute ROT is substantially lower (0.43 versus 1.24 degrees per minute).

plot.title: Direct-Nonstop Process and Kinematic Anomaly
plot.description: The anomaly bypasses the mid-sea anchorage and turns farther north; the point distributions compare its higher mean SOG and lower mean absolute ROT with the 11 typical voyages.

insights: The typical voyage process is stable across 11 trajectories: Under way using engine when leaving Harbour Orion, followed by an intermediate At anchor stage, Under way sailing, Restricted manoeuvrability on the approach to Harbour Lyra, and At anchor after arrival.

Every normal transition from Under way sailing to Restricted manoeuvrability contains a large course change. The turn redirects the vessel from its eastbound transit toward Harbour Lyra, where the final anchoring stage occurs.

voyage_12_direct_nonstop is the sole process anomaly. It does not anchor at the intermediate anchorage before arriving at Harbour Lyra, and its mean SOG is higher than for the typical voyages (10.19 versus 7.29 knots). Its turning point is farther north, so the final turn is milder and its mean absolute ROT is substantially lower (0.43 versus 1.24 degrees per minute).
summary: Across 11 repeated voyages, MV Aurora follows a stable five-stage sailing process with an intermediate anchorage and a large final harbour-approach turn. voyage_12_direct_nonstop is the only exception: it bypasses the intermediate anchorage, maintains a higher average SOG, and takes a farther-north, lower-ROT approach to Harbour Lyra.
